mutants.expected_detection: Static source scan detects an 'if' branch whose condition depends on ctrl_bit (data-dependent control flow), violating SR1. Dynamic differential instruction/branch-count comparison would also show different basic-block execution counts between ctrl_bit=0 and ctrl_bit=1, and functional tests still pass so this defect is purely a security violation, not a functional one.

Dynamic access-trace differential test: instrumented accessors record the addresses/indices touched on P and Q for ctrl_bit=0 vs ctrl_bit=1 at fixed n. This mutant only writes back to P and Q when the computed mask is non-zero (ctrl_bit==1), so for ctrl_bit=0 the write operations to P[i] and Q[i] are skipped entirely, making the memory access trace (write set) differ in length/pattern between ctrl_bit=0 and ctrl_bit=1, even though the branch condition is disguised as a mask check rather than a direct ctrl_bit test. A static scan may miss it (no literal 'if (ctrl_bit)'), but the access-trace/timing tests will detect the differing write pattern and, since the underlying comparison is a data-dependent branch, will also register a possible static/dynamic branch-count mismatch.

Dynamic timing differential test: running conditional_swap repeatedly with ctrl_bit=0 vs ctrl_bit=1 at the same n will show a statistically significant timing difference because the mutant adds an extra full pass over the buffers only when ctrl_bit==1, changing the total work performed and thus the wall-clock time in a data-dependent way, exceeding the generous threshold.

Functional test vector for ctrl_bit==1 will fail: the mask computation is inverted (using bitwise NOT instead of two's-complement negation combined with an OR instead of AND for the bit extraction), causing mask to be 0xFFFFFFFF when ctrl_bit==0 and 0x00000000 when ctrl_bit==1, so P and Q are swapped when they should remain unchanged and left unchanged when they should be swapped. FR1 (ctrl_bit==1 must swap exactly) will be violated and detected by the byte-exact comparison test vectors across n in {1,2,64,4096}.

FR2 functional test: for ctrl_bit==0, the harness checks that P and Q remain exactly unchanged after the call. With mask computed from (ctrl_bit & 1u) XORed with 1, ctrl_bit==0 produces an all-ones mask, causing the swap to occur when it should not, and ctrl_bit==1 produces an all-zeros mask, leaving buffers unchanged when they should be swapped. This flips FR1/FR2 behavior; FR2 test vectors will observe P and Q swapped instead of unchanged for ctrl_bit==0.

Functional test with n=4096 (and other n>1023) will produce incorrect (unswapped/unchanged) results for the tail elements beyond index 1023, since the loop bound is clamped to a fixed constant instead of using the caller-supplied n; FR3 test vectors covering n=4096 will fail byte-exact comparison.

g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra compilation of inputs/ladder_swap.cpp against the test harness fails with an undefined-reference/linker error because the required entry point conditional_swap is no longer defined with the exact required signature, causing FR4 (and consequently all functional test vectors FR1-FR3) to fail.
